A small note, folded and tucked into a rose bush. It reads: 'I left this for you. If you found it, I hope you smiled.'
A scrap of paper, pinned to a thorn: 'I pricked my finger on this bush. 0/10, would not recommend.'
A tiny note, hidden among the blueberries: 'These are the best berries in the forest. Please do not tell anyone.'
A note, tied to a stem with a blade of grass: 'The bees are planning something. I heard them buzzing about it.'
A small note, tucked under a stone at the base: 'I hid here once, when I was small. It was a good hiding spot.'
A crumpled note: 'If you are reading this, you have found my secret berry patch. Congratulations. Now go away.'
A tiny note, written in a very small hand: 'I once saw a fairy here. She was very small. She said hello.'
A note, written in faded berry juice: 'The rose hips are ready in autumn. Do not pick them all. Leave some for the birds.'
A small note, tucked into the lavender: 'I came here to calm down. It worked. Lavender is magic.'
A note, written in very neat handwriting: 'I picked three berries and left two. That is the rule.'
A sad little note: 'I planted this bush when I was young. I came back today. It is still here. So am I.'
A sweet note, folded into a tiny square: 'If you are reading this, know that someone once loved this bush. And now you do too.'
A note, written in a child's handwriting: 'I saw a bunny under this bush. He was very small. He had a lot of opinions.'
A note, written in a formal hand: 'NOTICE: This bush is under the protection of the local fairy council. Please do not disturb the flowers.'
A note, tucked into a fork: 'I ate too many berries. My stomach hurts. Worth it.'
A note, written in careful cursive: 'A bird built her nest here last spring. I watched her raise three chicks. I am a grandmother now, twice over.'
A tiny note, tied with a thread: 'I left this note for whoever finds this bush. Hello. I hope you are having a good day.'
A note, written in shaky handwriting: 'I am old now. This bush is older. We are both still blooming. That is enough.'
A note, written in a very official-looking script: 'By order of the squirrel council, all berries on this bush are subject to tax. This is a joke. Probably.'
A note, tucked into the gigglemint: 'I laughed for an hour after touching this bush. I do not know why. Best afternoon ever.'
A note, tucked into the whisperbush: 'I heard this bush whisper my name. It was very polite. It called me 'friend'.'
A note, tucked into the starbloom: 'I made a wish under this bush last night. I will not tell you what it was. But I think it will come true.'
